mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the prior quarter is interpreted by markets as a signal of tightening monetary policy, which reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the prior quarter
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 60-day rolling mean during tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment benefits applications (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in union membership proxies (not available in evidence) would suggest weaker labor market bargaining power, but since only PAYEMS is observable, its own monthly change predicts S&P 500 forward returns over 5 days: rising PAYEMS implies near-term labor market softening and lower equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > +5% from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day ahead returns remain positive despite sustained PAYEMS increases (p > 0.05 in walk-forward test).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of retail sales (not available) to GDP growth (GDPC1) turns positive, indicating stronger consumer demand relative to economic output, S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days are expected to be positive as markets anticipate sustained growth momentum.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under positive GDPC1 ratio are not statistically superior to baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 10% in two consecutive months signals supply-side softness that reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -10% from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite sustained INDPRO declines (p < 0.05 in test).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2% above prior month) combined with a hold in federal funds rates triggers a forward discounting effect, predicting negative S&P 500 20-day returns as markets price in higher future policy rates.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > +2% AND FEDFUNDS <= previous month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in unemployment (UNRATE below 4%) combined with rising housing starts (not available) would indicate labor market tightening, but using only UNRATE, its monthly decline below 4% predicts positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as investors anticipate growth from labor market strength.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not higher than the 20-day rolling mean during such periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of residential investment to GDP (not available) turns positive, indicating housing demand recovery, S&P 500 5-day forward returns are expected to be positive as market anticipates economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > +3% from prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain negative despite sustained HOUST increases (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the combined momentum of all observable macro proxies (GDPC1, CPIAUCSL, PAYEMS, INDPRO, RSAFS, UNRATE, HOUST, FEDFUNDS) is in the top quartile of their 12-month rolling distribution, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are predicted to be positive, reflecting broad-based economic optimism.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during such high-momentum periods (p > 0.05).
